steps.title: One factory for every layer skip group
notes: create_layer_skip_group adds the two parameters Expose every n-th layer (1 … 100) and Layer offset (0 … 99). The defaults 1 and 0 come from the library table: every layer is exposed.
The same function is called for every contour type, for every hatch group and for the wall supports, so all of them get the same two parameters.

steps.title: Read n and the offset
notes: read_layer_skip protects against n = 0 and takes the offset modulo n: with n = 2 the offsets 1 and 3 select the same layers. The drawing uses offset 3, which gives the same layers as offset 1.

steps.title: Counted from the part, not from the platform
notes: The layer index starts with 0 at the lowest layer of the part. ATU numbers its layers from 1, so for a part that starts on the platform, ATU's layer 101 is index 100.
That is why, in the video, n = 2 with offset 0 keeps the border on layers 101 and 103: index 100 and 102 are even.

steps.title: Yes or no for one layer
notes: is_active exposes a layer if index − offset is a multiple of n. It has no memory of earlier layers, so the answer is the same in every thread and in any order of the layers.
JavaScript's % keeps the sign of the left side, so a negative remainder is shifted up by n before the test.

lines: // No settings, or every_nth <= 1 (also undefined or NaN): expose every layer.
// A negative index should not happen. Exposing is the safe choice.
// Tip: % is the remainder of a division, e.g. 5 % 2 = 1.
// A remainder of 0 means the layer is one of the "every n-th" layers.
// In JavaScript the remainder has the sign of the dividend
// ((0 - 1) % 5 = -1), so it is shifted into [0, every_nth) first.

steps.title: Skip the whole vector type on that layer
notes: Each vector type asks is_active before it creates its paths: the first border, the following borders and fill contours, every hatch area and the wall supports. A skipped type produces nothing on that layer, there is no thinner or weaker version.
Different offsets make types take turns: here the border is on the odd layers, the hatch on the even layers. If every type is skipped on a layer, that layer stays empty.

recipes.title: Wall supports on every second layer by default
recipes.why: Supports only have to hold the part; exposing them on every second layer saves time and heat.
recipes.result: New profiles expose the wall supports on every second layer; the part itself is not affected.

recipes.title: Contours take turns
recipes.why: All contour types start with the same layer skip. Here every contour type starts with every second layer, so you can give the following borders offset 1 and let them alternate with the first border.
recipes.result: First border, following borders and fill contours start with Expose every n-th layer = 2. Try the same in the explainer with two different offsets.
